title: indian shares may fall crude hits 108 rising mideast risks 2026 09 11
text:
Sept 11 (Reuters) - Indian shares slid on Friday in a broad-based sell-off as intensifying Middle East conflict pushed Brent crude past $108 ​per barrel, raising concerns about the impact on inflation and ‌global interest rates.
The Nifty 50 (.NSEI)
, opens new tab
 dropped 0.92% to 23,261.7 and the BSE (.BSESN)
, opens new tab
 lost 0.84% to 74,272.61, as of 9:35 a.m. IST. Both indexes hit their lowest levels since June 11.
Fifteen ​of the 16 major sectors fell. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100)
, opens new tab
 and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100)
, opens new tab
 ​lost 1.2% and 1.4%, respectively.
Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port ⁠city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced down the Red Sea coast to ​strategic islands, military sources said, hours after President Donald Trump said he expected ​the Iran war to end after the U.S. midterm elections.
The move threatens Red Sea shipping, while tanker attacks have also intensified around the Strait of Hormuz.
Heavyweight financials (.NIFTYFIN)
, opens new tab
 fell 1.4%, ​while metals (.NIFTYMET)
, opens new tab
 and auto stocks (.NIFTYAUTO)
, opens new tab
 lost 2.8% and 1.3%, respectively.
Rising oil prices inflamed ​inflation risks and sent global bond yields to new highs, weighing on equities. MSCI's broadest ‌index ⁠for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS)
, opens new tab
 was down 1.8%.
"Financial markets are adjusting to a stronger probability of monetary tightening, with federal funds futures indicating a greater than 70% chance of a rate hike next week," said Devarsh Vakil, ​head of prime research ​at HDFC Securities.
Indian ⁠government bonds also plunged in opening deals on Friday, with the benchmark 10-year bond yield surpassing 7% to a ​more than three-month high as a combination of rising oil ​prices and ⁠higher U.S. yields hurt investor sentiment.
The Nifty 50 and Sensex are now down 2.7% and 2.9%, respectively, for the week, and on course for a fifth ⁠straight weekly ​drop.
Bucking the trend, ONGC (ONGC.NS)
, opens new tab
 and Oil India (OILI.NS)
, opens new tab
 ​jumped 1.3% and 0.7%, respectively, on Friday as higher crude prices tend to lift margins for upstream ​oil companies.
